session_notes:
SCOPE AND NOTATION. 16 runs of 03_resonator_spectroscopy_single, referenced here by their run number ("#5" = #5_03_resonator_spectroscopy_single_162158). All 16 are the NEW node generation: every params block carries min_dip_snr=6.0, dip_dominance=2.0, escalate_on_no_dip, max_escalation_span_in_mhz, and every fit carries dip_snr / ambiguous / candidates / success_shape. There is no old-generation run in this session, so "generation" never has to be disambiguated per case.

THE SINGLE BIGGEST STRUCTURAL FACT. escalate_on_no_dip was False in all 16 runs and max_escalation_span_in_mhz (800, later 1000) was therefore never spent once. The operator escalated instead by hand-editing the resonator RF_frequency in the live state between runs, which moves the sweep CENTRE. That manoeuvre is the source of nearly every wasted run and of both poisoned writes: this node fits the notch nearest the centre, so moving the centre onto a different notch produces a healthy-looking fit (success=True, success_shape=True, dip_snr in the teens, ambiguous=False) of the wrong resonance, with no flag raised anywhere.

TWO ENVIRONMENT FACTS THE CURSOR CANNOT SEE, WHICH HINDSIGHT SUPPLIES.
(1) Runs #8-#13 executed against a TRIMMED 4-qubit QUAM: quam_state/state.json in #12 and #13 contains only q10, q11, q15, q17. #14 onward reverts to the 13-qubit state in which those four are still at their design guesses (7000/6570/6800/7260 MHz). So #12's and #13's writes never reached the surviving state; they are a discarded branch.
(2) The flux operating point changed mid-session. The configuration in force from #29 to the end of the day (joint_offset: q9 -0.0850, q11 -0.0540, q15 -0.0540, q17 +0.1003 V) is the one the day's final state uses. #27 ran at a DIFFERENT configuration (q17 -0.0330, q5 +0.0270), which is why its q10/q15/q17 values sit 15-23 MHz below every neighbouring run; those writes were reverted before #29. #27's numbers are not wrong, they are not comparable, and treating them as a drift signal is the trap that run contains.

METHOD. I re-derived, from each run's ds_raw.h5, the amplitude trace, its background-divided prominence, the linear-detrended phase excursion and the IQ trajectory, for every run/qubit in scope; and I re-derived the flux-dependence maps from #26. That numeric cross-check is what settles which amplitude features are real resonances, and it is stronger than eyeballing. Figure budget used: 2 of 6 (#42 figures.amplitude.png and #42 figures.iq_circle.png), spent on the q15 adjudication.

WHAT THE FOUR-PANEL CROSS-CHECK ACTUALLY SHOWED. Both of q15's candidates (6801.3 and 6844.8 MHz) carry a genuine phase wrap (linear phase slope 15.0 and 16.4 deg/MHz) and both reach the IQ origin - so q15 is a true two-resonance ambiguity, not an amplitude artefact, and no setting of this node can resolve it. q17's two recurring values are the OPPOSITE case: in each individual panel only one of them exists (at #27 the 7313.1 position is flat, background-divided depth 0.03; at #41/#42 the 7290 position is flat, depth 0.11), so 7290/7313 is one flux-tunable resonator at two operating points, and the node was right never to flag q17 ambiguous.

THE FANO WARNING IS REAL HERE. In #42's amplitude panel the tallest excursion in the q4 sub-plot is the left-hand background at 7.46 GHz (~0.20 mV), not the notch at 7.5049 GHz (which reaches ~0.00 mV); q15 shows a 1.35 mV peak 6 MHz above its 6.802 GHz notch. This is why success_shape=False recurs for q4/q5/q6/q15 while the frequency is fine: it is a sloped-background artefact, not a wrong centre. A reader must not treat success_shape=False as "reject" - it is "the Lorentzian is a poor description", which is a different claim.

WHAT THE SESSION NEVER GOT. q15's and q11's own 06_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_flux failed on every attempt (#9, #10, #18, #25, #26). That is the measurement that would have assigned each of the paired notches to its owner by flux-tunability. Its absence is why q15 terminates unresolved and why q11's 49 MHz excursion was adjudicable only by SNR and reproducibility.

TOTALS. 13 targets. Ideal total 34 target-runs against an actual 106; two targets (q15, q2) end unresolved; 5 poisoned writes across q11, q15, q10 and q17, all of them traceable to a hand-moved sweep centre or to an abandoned flux configuration rather than to a bad fit.
adversarial_audit:
**Not sound. 17 defects; the load-bearing ones:**

**1. Session notes — the stated fit-selection mechanism is wrong.** "This node fits the notch nearest the centre." Six runs have >1 candidate; the only one where *nearest* and *strongest* disagree is #2/q4, and the node took idx 68 (prom 34.81, 8.2 MHz off centre) over idx 176 (prom 8.19, 2.6 MHz off centre). Selection is **max prom_snr**. Correct the mechanism; the poisoning is window *membership and edge distance*, not a proximity tie-break.

**2. q11 #33/#35 — consequent misdiagnosis.** Derived centres are 6633.761 / 6634.209, so 6585.161 sat **1.40 / 0.95 MHz inside the window edge** and drew **no candidate at all** — the same edge exclusion the key correctly diagnoses at #1/q3, not "passed over because it was not nearest the centre." Also #35's centre **equals #33's written value byte-exactly**: the poison propagated itself; no second hand-move occurred.

**3. Environment fact (2) is contradicted.** At #27 every centre is displaced and **restored byte-identically at #41**: q4 −16.000/+16.000, q6 −12.800/+12.800, q10 −22.000/+22.000, q5 −1.400, q9 −0.600. Each fit shift equals its own centre shift (q4 −15.54, q6 −12.84, q17 −23.18, q10 −21.01). A flux config "differing in q17 and q5" cannot do that. #27 is the key's own hand-moved-centre failure, exempted from its own diagnosis — which then excuses two poisoned writes as "correct measurements."

**4. Same claim, numerically false.** "#27's q10/q15/q17 sit 15-23 MHz below every neighbouring run": q15's #27 value is **+0.47 MHz** above #24's; q4 (−15.5) and q6 (−12.8) are omitted.

**5. #27 wrongly marked wasted.** For q9 it is 100 MHz/200 shots, shape True, unambiguous, offset unchanged — it meets every criterion used to terminate at #41, so **termination should be #27**, making #41 *and* #42 redundant. For q5 it is the **only** run ever to flag the 6782 MHz twin, which the key's own caveat calls the decisive gap.

**6. Totals.** Actual target-runs = **88**, not 106 (matches the key's own actual_length sum). Poisoned writes listed = **12** (10 excluding pre-run edits), not 5. q11 ran **eight** more times after #20, not nine.

**7. q10 #12 — unfair.** Step 1 prescribes "adopt / write," scores the operator "yes," then counts that write poisoned for a branch abandonment no future-blind operator could see. q11 and q17 wrote at the same #12 into the same branch and are not counted.

**8. q10/q11 ideal step 2 = #13.** #13 exists only from the forbidden hand-move; an ideal path cannot contain it. Ideal lengths → 2 and 3.

**9. Factual slips.** #42/q11 is not "the highest-quality fit in the session" (#2/q9: snr 165.6, r² 0.998 — the key says so itself). #1/q3's 612 kHz is not "4× narrower than every genuine candidate (2.1–3.3 MHz)": primaries run 1.844–3.340, and the key's own adopted q17 value (#20) is 1.844. The Fano paragraph lists q15 under "success_shape=False recurs" while citing #42, where q15 is **True** (also #17, #41).

**10. q17 story broken by #13.** Same trimmed branch, three minutes after #12, no flux calibration: centre 7289.8→7313.7, fit 7290.102→7314.900. Both positions in one flux configuration — dismissed as "contributed nothing."

**11. q2 free ride.** #5 serves the q1/q3/q7/q8 group whose power fix was #3/#4; the key puts q2's group's fix at #14–#16, i.e. after #5.

qubits.caveats: High confidence that q15 is unresolved; medium confidence on the physical interpretation of the pair. What is certain from the raw data is that both 6801.3 and 6844.8 MHz are real resonances present simultaneously at every flux configuration in the session, with comparable depth and comparable phase response - I verified this numerically in #27, #41 and #42 and visually in #42's amplitude and IQ-circle panels. What is NOT determinable from this family is which of them is q15's readout resonator; the chip carries more resonators than active qubits, and q15's flux sweep - the natural discriminator - failed five times out of five. Note the contrast with q17, where the same wide window shows only one notch present at a time: identical-looking history, opposite underlying cause.

qubits.caveats: q17 and q15 present the same surface history - two recurring values about 23 and 43 MHz apart, alternating between runs - and have opposite causes. For q17 the wide sweep settles it: only one notch exists in any given panel, so it is one flux-tunable resonator and the correct answer is simply 'whichever flux point you intend to operate at'. For q15 the identical wide sweep shows two notches simultaneously. Nothing short of looking at whether the rival position is empty distinguishes these two situations, and the node's own ambiguous flag does exactly that correctly here (False for q17, True for q15).
